compromised.note: standard pointing does not mark whether a shva is pronounced (/e/) or silent; the rules decide it from the shape of the word, which is right for most words but not all (a meteg, U+05BD, forces a heard shva). Prefixes are recognized only when followed by | (as in וּ|מַיִם). Qamats qatan is read as /o/ only before a hataf qamats or when written with U+05C7; otherwise qamats is /a/.

sub.comment: after a full vowel and a meteg, two tokens back
after the letter's vowel (or a shva), one token back
no vowel mark in this letter — the mark stays where it is
word-initial vav + shva is the conjunction — always /ve/
a shva marked heard — the meteg emits its /e/
any other shva — the placeholder ə, which the ipasub rules turn into e where it is heard and delete everywhere else
patah gnuva — het and ayin already emitted the fused /aħ/ or /aʕ/. He is not listed: it is silent, so its patah still sounds.
qamats qatan before a hataf qamats (צָהֳרַיִם)
alef is an onset before a vowel-bearing mater (גִּרְסָאוֹת)
em kri'a — a vowelless alef is silent for everyone (זֹאת, קָרָא)
patah gnuva — the /a/ is heard BEFORE the ayin (לֹעַ)

a word-final he is silent for everyone, mapiq or not (מוֹרֶה, אוֹתָהּ). Under a patah gnuva the patah still sounds, so גָּבוֹהַּ is ɡavoa — unlike het and ayin, which ARE pronounced there (שִׂיחַ → siaħ).
patah gnuva — the /a/ is heard BEFORE the het (שִׂיחַ)
a rafe — the stem's own fricative, final
a placeholder fricative the prefix rules may harden

a rafe — the stem's own fricative, final
a placeholder fricative the prefix rules may harden
ו׳ is /w/, as ג׳ is /dʒ/. marks.py writes it for a stem-initial וו (וואטסאפ), which is always /w/; a medial וו is ambiguous, so those words (טוויטר) get ו׳ from rules/vocalizations.tsv
first of a double vav is the consonant (עִוּוּת, עָווֹן)
after a shva, vav+holam is /vo/ not /o/ (לִגְוֹעַ)
shuruk — vav+dagesh carrying no vowel of its own
holam male — the vav is a mater, the holam gives /o/
a bare mid-word vav is a leftover mater (חֲתֻונָּה)
word-final -yv is /av/, the yod is silent (עַכְשָׁיו, סְתָיו)
ktiv male doubles the yod for a single consonant — חַיָּיל is χaˈjal. Hebrew has no /jj/, so the second one is silent.

the same word-finally (עֵינַיי ʕeˈnaj) — but only when the first yod carries no dagesh. A dagesh there is gemination and the final yod is the 1sg possessive, which IS pronounced: חַיַּי is ħaˈjaj, not ħaˈja.

yod kri'a — a bare mater after hiriq (לִירוֹת). The optional vav covers ktiv male, where a leftover mater sits between them (אֲוִויר → ʔaˈviᴚ). The optional bar covers a prefix whose hiriq absorbed a stem-initial yod: בִּ|ירוּשָׁלַיִם is biᴚuʃaˈlajim.

the same yod pointed with a silent shva, as the local model writes it: מִיְּרוּשָׁלַיִם is miᴚuʃaˈlajim, וִ|יְסַרְבֵּל visaᴚˈbel. A heard shva (meteg) keeps the yod; so does a doubled יי, where the shva'd yod follows the bare mater rather than the hiriq: סִייְּמָה is sijma.
... and after tsere, EXCEPT alef+tsere which is /ej/ (רֵיחַ vs אֵיתָנוּת)

ipasub.comment: the ole of a letter with a vowel and a meteg
the ole of a letter with a vowel, or a shva
any other — after aħ/aʕ, where the vowel token is fused
a patah gnuva never takes the stress: the syllable before it does (רוּחַ ˈᴚuaħ, שִׂיחַ ˈsiaħ)
the same under a mapiq he, which is silent, so its patah follows a vowel directly (גָּבוֹהַּ ɡaˈvoa)
otherwise the last syllable — milra, the Hebrew default
an ayin does not close a syllable before a yod: מַעְיָן maʕaˈjan, רַעְיוֹן ᴚaʕaˈjon. Ayin only — אַחְיָן is ʔaħˈjan
the conjunction is /ve/ where the pointing writes a shuruk before בומ״פ: וּ|מַיִם vemaˈjim. Needs the bar, which says the vav is the conjunction
a stem keeps its stop after a ב/ל prefix: לְ|בֵית is lebet, not the pointed levet. A rafe (the stem's own fricative, from the pipeline) gives a plain v, which this leaves alone
the same for כ (לְ|כִתָּה lekiˈta)
the same for פ (בְּ|פָרִיז bepaˈᴚiz)
and after the conjunction /ve/ before a labial: וּ|בֵית vebet. Not before other letters — וְ|כָתַבְתִּי is veχatavti
the same for פ (וּ|פֹה vepo)
a ב prefix behind another prefix keeps its stop: וּבַ|מַּיִם vebamaˈjim, not the pointed vevamajim
... and its vowel: וּבְ|בַת vebebat, וּבְ|כִתָּה vebekiˈta (with the stop alone this was uvkiˈta)
a kaf hardens before a het rather than give /χχ/: הִכְחִיל hikˈχil. A het before a kaf does not (חָכָם)
under a sonorant or yod (רְכִישָׁה ᴚeχiˈʃa)
before an alef, ayin or he (שְׁאֵלָה ʃeʔeˈla)
under a one-letter prefix, ו כ ל ב (בְּ|בַיִת)
a stem's sonorant, as for the word (הַ|יְּלָדִים)
a stem's shva before a guttural, as for the word
of two shvas in a row the first closes a syllable and the second is heard (יִשְׁמְרוּ jiʃmeᴚu) — but not word-finally, where the two are a coda cluster (כָּתַבְתְּ katavt)
two copies of one consonant cannot cluster, so the cluster breaks: הִתְמוֹדְדוּ hitmodeˈdu, הִבַּטְתִּי hiˈbateti (ט against ת). A dagesh is plain gemination and is not broken: מִמְּךָ mimˈχa
the same letter twice is a collision even where the dagesh makes one a stop and the other a fricative: חִבְּבוּ ħibeˈvu
... the other way round
... and for פ
... both ways
a /d/ closing a syllable before a /t/ is near enough a geminate to go the same way: מָדַדְתִּי maˈdadeti, לָמַדְתִּי laˈmadeti. Any other pair is sayable (סָבַבְתִּי saˈvavti)

a stem that starts with a silent shva has a two-consonant onset, and the stress goes before both: הַ|שְּׁנַיִם haˈʃnajim. Not after a sonorant, which closes the prefix's syllable instead (שֶׁ|לְּךָ ʃelˈχa)
every shva no rule claimed is silent
... the first token too, behind a silent letter
a ב/כ/פ no prefix rule claimed is the fricative
the prefix bar has done its work
... the first token too
word-initial cluster — stress moves to the very front
a word that starts with its stressed vowel — a lone shuruk וּ — has no onset to walk back over; the mark still goes first
the same when the default stress put the mark before that first vowel
a stressed patah gnuva is emitted as one /aħ/ or /aʕ/ token, so the mark lands after it; put it back in front (שִׂיחַ → siˈaħ)
otherwise stress moves left over one onset consonant
a patah gnuva is emitted fused, because the vowel is heard before the consonant — but they are two segments, so split them once the stress rules have used the fused form
a word-final yod is the offglide of a diphthong, not a phoneme of its own — שַׁי is ʃ+aj, where בַּיִת is b+a+j+i+t
the same before a consonant (נַיְט najt)
a word-final yod after hiriq is not a separate glide
